entries.motif: sealed chutney jar with a pocket watch at midnight, on manuscript pages
entries.motifRationale: Midnight's Children: Saleem preserves history in pickle jars — the novel names it the 'chutnification of history' — and the narrator is born at the exact midnight of independence. Jar + midnight watch are the book's own emblem pair.
entries.iconographyNote: Living author — face generation prohibited (rung 3 bright line). Still-life frontispiece: the object sits in the portrait's place (thesis ④-3). VAD rejected v1: the watch leaked the stock 10:10 convention — for this motif the midnight hands ARE the content. v2 fused jar and clock; v3 pinned a single timepiece with merged hands at 12.
entries.prompt: Antique copperplate engraving, still-life frontispiece: two separate objects on a writing desk with loose manuscript pages. On the left, a clear glass jar filled with dark chutney, sealed with waxed cloth tied by twine. On the right, clearly apart from the jar, one single open pocket watch lying flat, its dial fully visible, hour hand and minute hand merged into one line pointing straight up at the 12 — exactly twelve o'clock, midnight. Only one timepiece in the whole image. Dense crosshatching and stipple shading, monochrome black ink on aged cream paper, engraved book-frontispiece line work, plain vignette background fading to paper. Intimate, mythic, restrained. No frame, no text, no signature, not photorealistic.

entries.motif: muted post horn resting on undelivered letters
entries.motifRationale: The Crying of Lot 49: the muted post horn is the Trystero/W.A.S.T.E. emblem — the novel's central symbol, and the fitting mark for literature's most famously unseen author.
entries.iconographyNote: Living author — face generation prohibited (rung 3 bright line; also the author's own lifelong refusal of portraiture makes the object-portrait the honest form). v2 pinned the wooden mute onto the horn.
entries.prompt: Antique copperplate engraving, still-life frontispiece: an old brass post horn shown in strict side profile, coiled once, its bell opening pointing to the right and plugged shut by a large round wooden mute stopper that visibly fills and silences the bell mouth. The silenced horn rests centered like a bust upon a small stack of undelivered letters with dark wax seals. Dense crosshatching and stipple shading, monochrome black ink on aged cream paper, engraved book-frontispiece line work, plain vignette background fading to paper. Conspiratorial, quiet. No frame, no text, no signature, not photorealistic.
